_doc: THE TEMPLATE CHECK CATALOGUE. After a conversion, TemplateCheck.js reads what the conversion already produced — the run notes, the notes printed in the pages (class cv2-note) and the un-built interactive boxes (class cv2-interactive cv2-int-ref) — and turns the things PageForge was unsure about into a short list of plain-English questions for the developer, grouped into the sections below. This file holds every question: which notes it matches (a regex over the note's text, with named groups for the blanks), how the matches are grouped, the question's wording with {blanks}, and the answer choices. The code only matches, fills in blanks and renders. Answers are recorded in the {CODE}_template-answers.json file; they change no page. The entries are tried in the order they are listed (the first match wins); the panel shows them by section. Every question gets a Skip button and a comment box from the renderer. A template that is a list is read in order: the first one whose blanks are all filled is used.

sections.title: Things only you know
sections.description: Facts a Writers Template never holds, such as links and quicklinks. Answer once for the whole module.

sections.title: Things the template got wrong
sections.description: Places where the writer's tags don't fit together. PageForge kept the content, but not in the shape the writer meant.

sections.title: Guesses to confirm
sections.description: Decisions PageForge made on its own. Please check them against the Writers Template.

sections.title: Requests the writer made to you
sections.description: The writer's notes to the developer, word for word. Tick each one once you've seen it.

sections.title: Not in the template
sections.description: Things the pages need that this Writers Template doesn't contain, so PageForge can't do them.

sections.title: Interactives PageForge will hand off
sections.description: Interactives PageForge couldn't build. They're listed so you know what's coming. There's nothing to answer.

sections.title: Other things PageForge noticed
sections.description: Anything else PageForge flagged, in its own words. For information only.

_meta.request_words: \?|\b(can we|could we|could you|can you|please|is it possible|are we able|would like|designer note|note to designer|dev(eloper)? note|replace|insert .{0,40} from|same (image|as)|use the same|something like|mock ?up|similar to)\b

page_notes._doc: How a page note is found and read: the paragraph's text after its prefix is what the match patterns see (tags stripped, entities decoded, line breaks as spaces).

activity_renumbered._doc: A run note saying PageForge renumbered a page's activities maps a page's activity back to the writer's number, so a question can name both.

forms: Page {page}, activity {activity} ({writer_activity} in the Writers Template)

plurals._doc: Filled from a number blank: {s} and the others follow {count}; for any other number blank X they are {X_s}, {X_es} and so on.

article._doc: {type_article}: «an» before a type name that starts with a vowel, «a» before the rest.

ignore._doc: PageForge reporting its own normal work, not questions. These — and every info-level run note no question claims — are only counted: «PageForge handled N small things automatically».

other._doc: What nothing above claims and is not ignored: a warn or error run note, or a Red Flag / To Do page note, is listed in section 7 in PageForge's own words. A Writers Note that is not a request is only counted.
